title: Television: fast-scan and SSTV
blurb: Explain NTSC interlace, vestigial sideband, digital TV coding rates and how SSTV encodes brightness, color and line starts.

E2B01.why: Rate 3/4 means **3 of every 4 bits are data** and the other 1 in 4 (**25%**) is forward error correction.
E2B01.trap: It is not compression and not a guard interval.

E2B02.why: An NTSC frame is **525 lines**. The 30 and 60 numbers are frames and fields per second.
E2B02.trap: 1080 is an HD format, not NTSC.

E2B03.why: Interlace scans the **odd-numbered lines in one field, then the even-numbered lines** in the next.
E2B03.trap: Every line still runs left to right.

E2B04.why: Analog SSTV sends **color lines sequentially**, one color scan after another.
E2B04.trap: There is no color burst or subcarrier as in NTSC.

E2B05.why: VSB **reduces bandwidth** while keeping good **low-frequency video fidelity**.
E2B05.trap: It carries neither audio nor chroma.

E2B06.why: VSB is AM sending **one complete sideband and part of the other**.

E2B07.why: DVB-T amateur TV is modulated with **QAM and QPSK**.
E2B07.trap: FM, FSK, AM and OOK are not DVB-T modulation.

E2B08.why: 70 cm overlaps **channels shared with cable TV**, so a cable-ready analog TV can tune it directly.

E2B09.why: DRM SSTV is an audio signal, so a plain **SSB receiver** can receive and decode it.

E2B10.why: In analog SSTV, **tone frequency** encodes brightness: a low pitch is dark, a high pitch is bright.
E2B10.trap: Amplitude does not carry the picture.

E2B11.why: The VIS code identifies **which SSTV mode** is being sent, so the software can set itself up.
E2B11.trap: It isn't line sync or the call sign.

E2B12.why: **Specific tone frequencies** (the sync tone) mark the start of each line.
E2B12.trap: Timing alone or amplitude is not used.
